summary: Chair merge of the second-pass lists: 7 items (2 fix-this-rev copper/text, 1 fix-this-rev ATP text, 2 next-rev with this-rev probes, 2 accept-with-rationale). Both principals and the verifier agree the six first-review fixes are applied correctly and introduced no failure or damage path: item 1 JP510.1 = CHG_SYS; item 2 J14.1 In1 stub present and the J16.8 path removed; item 3 sense loop 7.8 mOhm with Kelvin VSS; item 4 C513 at the SYS pins, 9 EP PTH pads, GND via at every charger cap; item 6 bench_power_width rule present; item 7 18 V text, OVP procedure and silk legends at J400/J401. The one disagreement (J510 severity/disposition) is decided for QA: the chair retrieved the HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (LCSC C165948, flux.ai mirror) and read RECOMMEND P.C.B LAYOUT directly: PCB EDGE is 5.79 mm from the 0.60 peg-hole centre, with the 4.18 slot pitch, 0.50 slot-to-peg, 2.60 face-to-front-leg and 6.77 face-to-rear-leg all matching the KiCad footprint, so HRO places the shell face 0.46 mm proud of the edge and J510 (face 2.41 mm behind Edge.Cuts y=172.12) is 2.87 mm deeper than recommended and 1.2 mm deeper than the flown J12 that is known to mate. That is a plausible Mode-2 functional failure with ordinary cables, fixable by a bench-area-only move into a strip that holds no tracks or vias inside the J510 courtyard width (three 0.8 mm vias at y=169.1, x=250.65/254.8/268.95, sit outside it; QA's 'no vias' wording was slightly wrong, the conclusion holds). J500 over-voltage (text + legend) and the TP503/TP504 ATP reference wording are the other this-rev actions, all text. Two rework regressions (REGN/BTST cap routing, C216 via-less island) stay next-rev with probes added to the existing item-4 and item-5 gates. Mode 2 ISS bypass and the inner-layer bench runs are accepted with a note. Dropped: C215/C218 swap (inside item 5; probe folded into the C216 item), starved_thermal hygiene (next-rev .kicad_pro note only), the refuted FT-GPIO pull-up entry.

items.title: J510 charger USB-C face sits 2.41 mm behind the board edge, 2.87 mm deeper than the HRO drawing's PCB EDGE line; a standard plug overmold stops ~2 mm short of seating, so Mode 2 may not work with ordinary cables
items.location: FlatSat_V1.kicad_pcb: J510 Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12 at (262.0,166.06) rot 0 F.Cu; pegs rel (+-2.89,-2.6), rear slots rel y -3.13, front slots rel y +1.05, F.Fab front rel +3.65 = abs y 169.71, courtyard 170.24; Edge.Cuts bottom line y=172.12 (x 147.343-292.39, straight). Compare flown J12 (223.16,78.6) recess 1.19 mm and J701 (275,51.874) rot 180 recess 0.64 mm. HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (LCSC C165948, 2020-12-08, sheet 1): RECOMMEND P.C.B LAYOUT, PCB EDGE = 5.79 from the 0.60 peg-hole centre; 4.18 slot pitch, 0.50 rear-slot-to-peg, side view 2.60 face-to-front-leg and 6.77 face-to-rear-leg.
items.rationale: PCB principal left this 'uncertain / next-rev' because the drawing could not be retrieved; QA read it as 5.79 mm. The chair retrieved and read the drawing (storage.googleapis.com graviton mirror of the LCSC PDF, rendered page 1) and confirms QA: PCB EDGE 5.79 mm from the peg-hole centre, and every other dimension (4.18, 0.50, 2.60, 6.77, 5.78 peg spacing, 8.65 slot span) matches the KiCad footprint, so the footprint origin is trustworthy and HRO intends the shell face 0.46 mm proud of the edge. J510's face is 2.41 mm behind the edge: 2.87 mm deeper than recommended and 1.22 mm deeper than the flown J12, the worst case known to mate. The 3.26 mm shell puts the plug axis 1.63 mm above the board, so any overmold taller than ~3.3 mm meets the 1.6 mm FR4 lip after about 6.65-2.41 = 4.24 mm of insertion, short of the latch and contact wipe; result is no latch and intermittent or absent VBUS at the 1.48 A ILIM, i.e. Mode 2 (the SYS feed item 1 just moved the FC onto) unusable with ordinary cables. That meets the PM's fix-this-rev test (bench board fails) even though a workaround exists (TP510 VBUS_CHG/GND breakout or a slim-overmold cable) and nothing is damaged. The fix is confined to the bench area: the chair re-checked the strip south of J510 and found no tracks on any layer in x 255-270, y 166.5-172.5 and no vias inside the courtyard width x 256.7-267.3 (three 0.8 mm vias at y=169.1 sit at x 250.65, 254.8 and 268.95, 1.6-1.9 mm outside it); only J510's own five F.Cu escapes (x 259.55-264.45, y 155.6-163.2) and the GND fill change. J510 is outside FC_COPY so heritage.py is unaffected. Not introduced by the six fixes; the first pass missed it.
items.action: Before gerbers: move J510 to (262.0,168.93) (F.Fab front y=172.58, 0.46 mm proud per HRO; rear courtyard y=163.66), or at minimum (262.0,168.47) for a flush face; extend the VBUS_CHG/CC/D+/D-/GND escapes by the same 2.41-2.87 mm, refill zones, re-run DRC (expect only the known residuals) and heritage.py (expect 0). Front slot pads land at y~170.0, 1.3 mm inside the edge, so copper_edge_clearance stays clean. If the owner declares the gerbers frozen: accept this rev with the TP510/GND breakout written into the Mode 2 procedure and a slim-overmold cable in the kit, and move J510 next rev. A 1:1 print test fit of the actual bench cable is a free cross-check either way.
items.verification: After the edit: pad-net dump shows J510 F.Fab front >= Edge.Cuts y (flush or proud), DRC 0 new items, heritage.py 0 violations. Pre-order: 1:1 paper print, bench USB-C cable overmold clears the paper edge before the shell line. After build: audible latch, VBUS_CHG at TP510 holds 5.0 V within 50 mV of the cable's open end at ILIM 1.48 A, no dropouts in a wiggle test, Mode 2 bring-up on an ordinary cable.

items.title: J500 bench-PSU input has no over-voltage element, no OVP trip procedure and no voltage legend; the R5460 trip does not block PSU current into FC-copy 10 V caps, U500 and IC6 through the Q501 body diode
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch: J500.1 = Dir_Chrg_In -> R109 -> VBATT_SENSE (C42, IC6 LT3652 BAT) -> inhibit shunts -> VBUSP (C1, C3); R500 330R -> U500 VDD; Q501 S = B-, D = PROT_DRAIN; text lines 13223 (window 4.9-8.4 V), 13267 (8.4 V or less), 13300 (floating), 13179 (never fit JP510 with a PSU). PCB: J500 MKDS 1x03 at (202.92,165.2); J400/J401 MKDS 1x02 at (228.96/241.46,165.3) on the same row; F.SilkS '18V MAX' at (233.0,171.2) and (245.5,171.2) only; no gr_text at y>167 for x 190-230.
items.rationale: Both principals rank 1, minor, fix-this-rev, trivial; verifier confirmed. Above VDET1 (8.5 V) the R5460 opens COUT, but PSU current into the FC copy is discharge-direction for the pack model (FC GND -> ISS shunt -> B- -> Q501 source-to-drain, the NMOS body-diode forward direction), so Dir_Chrg_In, VBATT_SENSE and (shunts closed) VBUSP see V_PSU - 0.7 V. C42/C1/C3 are C19702 10 uF 10 V X5R; U500 R5460 VDD abs max 12 V (operating 10 V, EA-165); IC6 LT3652 BAT abs max 15 V. The bench already runs 12-18 V on J400/J401 16 mm away in the same Phoenix family, and first-review item 7 gave those terminals an OVP pre-session check and an '18V MAX' legend; J500 got neither. A shorted FC-copy MLCC would dump PSU current (2 A limit) into frozen FC copper, the outcome this board must avoid. Operator error against a documented window, same class and precedent as item 7: text-only mitigation this rev. The BQ25886 SYS 12 V sub-case needs JP510 fitted with a PSU on J500, already forbidden at line 13179, so it adds nothing. Not a re-report: items 7/9/10 never raised J500 over-voltage.
items.action: Sheet note beside the BENCH PSU WINDOW line and bench procedure: 'PSU OVP <= 9 V; verify the trip with J500 disconnected before each session; never use the 12-18 V VSOLAR supply on J500 (heritage C42/C1/C3 are 10 V rated, U500 VDD abs max 12 V).' F.SilkS '8.4V MAX' 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm at (208.0,171.2) in the style of the J40x legends (row empty for x 195-225); if rank 1 reopens the PCB file this legend goes in the same edit, otherwise a sticker on the built boards. Fold the Mode 2 ISS-bypass line (rank 6) into the same sheet edit. Next rev: OV cut-off on J500.1 (Zener-gated PMOS or OVP load switch opening ~9 V) ahead of the J14 stub, shared with the first-review item 9 reverse-polarity element.
items.verification: Sheet grep shows the OVP line next to the window; bench procedure lists the pre-session J500 OVP trip check (raise PSU with J500 open, trip <= 9 V); legend present on the built boards. No ATP step catches a mis-set PSU after the fact, so the gate is the pre-session trip check plus the legend. Next rev: netlist shows an OV switch between J500.1 and Dir_Chrg_In, trip test 9-9.5 V with the FC copy unpowered.

items.title: Item-3 ATP points the scope at TP503/TP504, which are referenced to floating VBAT_BENCH_N (TP501) and B- (TP502), not GND; an earthed scope ground there with J701 or FC USB on a PC bypasses Q500/Q501 and invalidates the 2 A no-latch and trip tests
items.location: battery_protection_replica: TP501 VBAT_BENCH_N (194.0,163.5) = U500.6 VSS = Q500 S; TP503 DOUT_GATE (U500.1, Q500.4) referenced to VSS; TP504 COUT_GATE (U500.2, Q501.4) low level = V-/B- (TP502) per R5460 EA-165 p.9; J500.3 silk 'B-' at (213.08,163.0) is VBAT_BENCH_N; TP500-TP505 cluster has no GND point; J701 A1/B1/S1 = GND; sheet line 13300 warns only about an earthed PSU negative; docs/reviews/2026-10-21_FlatSat_V1/final_list.md item 3 verification text.
items.rationale: Packet id 14, verifier confirmed, both principals info. PCB said next-rev, QA fix-this-rev; the chair takes fix-this-rev because both actions say 'amend the ATP now' and the wording must be in place before the first Mode-1 trip test, which is this rev's ATP. VBAT_BENCH_N reaches GND only through Q500/Q501/B- and the inhibit; clipping a scope ground to TP501 or to the pin silk-screened 'B-' is the natural move and, with board GND earthed through J701 or FC USB, the earth loop parallels the FETs: before a trip it diverts ~10-30 % of load current (biasing the 2 A no-latch criterion toward a pass), after a DOUT trip it keeps the FC powered through probe shield and USB GND. No damage at the 2 A PSU limit, no copper change. The original finding's 'both gates referenced to VSS' is corrected: COUT_GATE pairs with B- (TP502).
items.action: ATP and bench procedure: 'TP501/TP503 are referenced to VBAT_BENCH_N and TP502/TP504 to B-, not GND. Measure gate drive with a floating DMM, a differential probe or an isolated scope; or clip the scope ground to board GND (JP607.2) with JP607 closed and read gates relative to TP501/TP502 by subtraction. Never earth TP501 or J500.3 while J701 or FC USB is on an earthed host.' Next rev: GND test point in the TP500-TP505 cluster and silk 'VBAT_N' instead of 'B-' at J500.3.
items.verification: ATP text shows the reference statement and the floating-measurement method. Item-3 gate: current into J500.1 equals current out of J500.3 within 2 % at 2.0 A (no earth-loop diversion); DOUT/COUT gates high at 2.0 A; a deliberate excess-discharge trip drops TP500 Dir_Chrg_In to 0 V within the R5460 delay instead of the FC staying up.

items.title: BQ25886 gate-drive caps not at their pins: REGN C516 rotated with its GND pad toward pin 11 (7.0 mm, two vias via In1); item-4 move of C512 lengthened the BTST trace 3.8 -> 7.8 mm on B.Cu (bootstrap loop area no worse)
items.rationale: Packet ids 2 and 10 merged by both principals, both verifier-confirmed minor, identical disposition. REGN is the real deviation and predates the rework: the 4.7 uF sits 3.3 mm from the pin but connects through ~7 mm of 0.25 mm track and two 0.46/0.20 vias cut into the In1 GND plane because its GND pad faces the IC; a 180-degree rotation gives 1.3-1.8 mm of F.Cu with no via. This is the hard-switched low-side driver supply, the half that matters. BTST grew because item 4 freed the SYS-pin slot for C513 (TI priority 1 over priority 4, a correct trade), but the same move cut the SW leg from ~7.7 mm x 0.25 mm to ~2.3 mm x 0.8 mm, so the pin12-C512-pin17/18 loop is about the same length and encloses less area, and the high-side FET in a boost stage is the soft-switched synchronous rectifier. Expected effect a few nH and sub-volt REGN bounce, far from the 6 V abs max; no REGN UVLO specified. No failure or damage path, so next-rev with a probe added to the item-4 scope gate that already exists. Item 4 otherwise verified complete.
items.action: This rev: no copper change by default; add to the item-4 scope gate (ILIM 1.48 A via R514 750R, VBUS 5.25 V, SYS loaded) REGN at C516.1 referenced to C516.2 with a ground spring and the BTST-SW differential at C512. Owner's option only if rank 1 reopens the PCB file: rotate C516 180 degrees and re-route REGN on F.Cu in the same bench-area edit. Next rev: rotate C516 so pad 1 faces pin 11, route REGN ~1.5 mm on F.Cu with no via, delete the In1 REGN segment, give C516.2 its own GND via; place C512 at the south-east corner between pin 12 and pins 17/18 so the BTST and SW legs are each under 3 mm on F.Cu.
items.verification: Bench: SW pin 17 peak < 11 V (existing item-4 limit), REGN 4.7-5.15 V with ripple < 200 mVpp and no excursion below 4.5 V, BTST-SW peak < 5.7 V, no sustained ringing > 3 cycles at the switching edge; out-of-band result -> derate ILIM via R514 and promote the C516 rotation. Next rev: pad-net dump shows REGN pin 11 -> C516.1 <= 2 mm with 0 vias, BTST pin 12 -> C512.2 <= 3 mm; DRC clean.

items.title: Via-in-pad batch b1 left C216.2 (DVDD pin-23 4.7 uF) and Y200.4 on a via-less F.Cu GND island; core return runs ~6 mm of 0.25 mm trace across the crystal case pads
items.rationale: Packet id 5, verifier confirmed with an F.Cu-only connectivity check; both principals minor / next-rev. Owner rulings F16/F17 freed every via-in-pad; batch b1 removed the Y200.4 in-pad GND via and left the island's only exit a diagonal 0.25 mm link to Y200.2, so the pin-23 cap return grows from ~2 mm to ~6 mm (~1.2 nH, 1-2x the mounted ESL of an 0402 4.7 uF) and core transient return current crosses the crystal case pads inside the oscillator guard. Worse than both the pre-rework board and the flown U18 pin-23 cell (C70 with a GND via 0.85 mm away in a 13-via pour); emulator_replace.md records '~4 mm instead of 1.6 mm' but not the missing via. Impact is small: this is the datasheet's 'for best performance' second 4.7 uF, COUT and C218 at pin 39 are unaffected, and only mV-level GND current crosses the crystal link. No failure shown; candidate via spots are blocked by In2 1V1_EMU, B.Cu EMU_SWCLK and F.Cu EMU_UART_RX/EMU_XOUT, so there is no free this-rev fix. Folded into the item-5 bench gate; the C215/C218 pin-46 probe from QA's rank 7 is folded here too rather than carried as its own item.
items.action: This rev: no copper change. Item-5 bring-up gate adds (a) 1V1_EMU at C216.1/pin 23 with a short ground to C216.2 alongside TP202, at idle and under the 0 -> 150 mA core step, and (b) VREG_AVDD_EMU at pin 46 vs C215.1 during the same step. Next rev, with the item-5 copy of the flown U18 cell: give C216.2 its own off-pad GND via (or move C216 so pad 2 lands in the main pour with an adjacent via), remove the Y200.4 -> Y200.2 link so core return stays off the crystal pads, restore a stitched crystal GND pour as on U18, and put CFILT adjacent to pin 46 on F.Cu with R200 upstream (flown C68/R94).
items.verification: Bench: pin-23 1V1 ripple and load-step excursion within 20 % of TP202 and no worse than ~2x the FC copy's +1V1 under the same step; pin-46 HF content no more than a few mV above C215.1; crystal start-up and frequency unaffected (EMU USB enumerates, SysTick/clock check). Next rev: F.Cu connectivity check shows the island containing C216.2 holds >= 1 GND via within 1 mm of the pad; U200-vs-U18 parity check extended to pin-23 decoupling.

items.title: Mode 2 (USB charger) returns through board GND, so the ISS inhibit chain (J15/J19/JP607) and the R5460 replica are out of the FC power path; sheet and pyro POWER-UP RECIPE do not say so
items.location: battery_protection_replica.kicad_sch lines 13102 (B- note) and 13201 (Mode 2 line); pyro_inhibit.kicad_sch ~4165 POWER-UP RECIPE ('bridge JP607 (B- return) + JP606 (RBF) + ONE inhibit path'). Netlist: U511 pins 4/19/20/25 = GND, J510 GND; JP510.1 = CHG_SYS, JP510.2 = Dir_Chrg_In; B- = Q501.1-3, J14.2/4/6/8, J15.1, J19.1/3, JP607.1 (no GND member); JP607.2/J15.2/J19.2/4 = GND.
items.rationale: Packet ids 4 and 13 merged by both principals, both verifier-confirmed and downgraded to info. PCB said next-rev, QA accept-with-rationale; the chair takes accept-with-rationale because the topology is accepted as inherent to any GND-referenced source (heritage solar via the LT3652 and FC USB J12/D15 bypass the ISS inhibit the same way, and the pyro sheet already warns about J12) and the only action is a note. It was not introduced by fix item 1 (the old CHG_BAT feed was equally GND-referenced). The high-side S1/S2/P1/P2/RBF chain and SW600 still act, so JP606/RBF still safes the bus; an ISS-open check run in Mode 2 fails visibly rather than passing silently. No hardware risk at 8.4 V / 1.48 A. Residue: the pyro recipe presents JP607 as required for power, true only in Mode 1, and nothing tells a bench user to run inhibit tests in Mode 1.
items.action: One line in the Mode 2 sheet note (13201), the pyro POWER-UP RECIPE and the bench procedure, bundled with the rank-2 sheet edit: 'Mode 2 returns through board GND: the ISS inhibit (J15/J19/JP607) and the R5460 replica are NOT in circuit; JP607 is needed in Mode 1 only; safe the bus with JP606/RBF; run ISS-inhibit, deployment-switch and protection-trip tests in Mode 1 only.' No hardware change; a B--referenced (isolated) charger return is not worth the cost.
items.verification: Sheet grep shows the Mode 2 exemption on both sheets; the bench procedure's inhibit-matrix section is tagged Mode 1 only. ATP sanity check: in Mode 2 with JP607 pulled the FC stays up (expected); with JP606 pulled VBUSP collapses.

items.title: Mode-1 bench current passes through three series 0.5 oz inner-layer runs at 1.0-1.1 mm (new item-2 In1 stub, B- In2/In1, VBAT_BENCH_N In2); bench_power_width rule is not layer-aware
items.rationale: Packet id 11; both principals info / accept-with-rationale; verifier confirmed the geometry and series topology but refuted the thermal consequence. At the 2 A PSU limit each run dissipates 35-52 mW (~3.9 mW/mm) and sits 0.21 mm from a GND plane, so realistic rise is ~10 C; the IPC-2221 internal curve (86-102 C) does not apply to short traces next to planes and the 20 C IR criterion belonged to the removed heritage J16.8 path. Total ~31 mOhm (~60 mV at 2 A) matches item 2's 34.7 mOhm J500.1 -> J14.1 figure. The In1 stub meets the item-2 action ('>= 1.0 mm, any layer') and review_fixes.md records why In1 was the only free layer at J14.1; the B- and VBAT_BENCH_N runs are unchanged since the first review accepted them. The brief-L5 'on F.Cu/B.Cu' wording is an internal-brief deviation, not a failure mechanism; no 1.5 A interim cap is needed. Recorded so the item-2 IR check covers these runs and the rule gap is not lost.
items.action: No this-rev change and no current cap; record the rationale in review_fixes.md. Include the three inner runs in the existing item-2 IR check. Next rev, optional: add a layer condition to bench_power_width (2.0 mm minimum on In1/In2 for BenchPower/FCPower, or 1.0 mm outer only) or keep bench power on outer layers per brief L5 where routing allows.
items.verification: Item-2 IR run: 2 A for 10 min, all three runs < 20 C rise (expect < 15 C) with no hotspot above the known 0.3 mm F.Cu VBAT_BENCH_N neck; J500.1 -> J14.1 drop <= 70 mV at 2 A. Next rev: DRC with the layer-aware rule reports 0 inner-layer BenchPower runs under 2.0 mm.

dropped: Packet id 3 / QA rank 7 (VREG_AVDD C215/C218 swap lengthened the pin 46 -> CFILT path 3.56 -> 5.7 mm with two In2 vias): verifier downgraded to info; the LX-adjacent via sits 1.27 mm from LX in both topologies, C215 is the HF shunt either way, R200's 33 ohm plays no part at fF-coupling frequencies, and the rework removed the AVDD In2 run under the L200 LX pad edge, so net exposure is no worse. Already documented in emulator_replace.md and inside first-review item 5 (monitor-in-test); PM instruction not to re-report item 5 unless the rework made it worse. The pin-46 probe is folded into rank 5's item-5 gate so nothing is lost.

Packet id 9 / QA rank 9 (starved_thermal = ignore in FlatSat_V1.kicad_pro, 57 single-spoke items, 26 new in the bench area, drc_triage.md says '0, fixed'): both verifiers found no electrical or JLC manufacturability consequence (setting byte-identical to flown Rev2; U511 PGND 19/20 bridged on F.Cu into the solid-connected 9-via EP with their own GND via; pin 5 is the OTG strap; J510/J701 GND pads lose < 1 mV at 1.48 A through ~0.5 mOhm spokes beside the shell PTH; J19.4's isolated B.Cu spoke is on a PTH pad connected on other layers). Hygiene note carried here for next rev: set starved_thermal to 'warning' in .kicad_pro, correct the drc_triage.md line (the claim is vacuous while the check is ignored), and give the USB-C GND pads and C516.2 a solid connection or a via.

Refuted entry (always-on +3V3 pull-ups into six U200 GPIOs with J701 absent): the pins are RP2350 failsafe (FT) IOs within 3.63 V abs max at IOVDD = 0; the emulator sheet already documents the phantom path and its BENCH RULE (plug J701 before or with FC power); the proposed R600 move to 3V3_EMU would hold FC-commanded Deploy EN at ~1.8 V, below the TPS4H160 VIH 2.0 V, when the emulator is unpowered, reversing a chair-accepted fix. No defect.

Merged, not dropped: ids 4 and 13 (Mode 2 ISS bypass) into rank 6; ids 2 and 10 (BQ25886 REGN/BTST) into rank 4. Sub-claims dropped on the way: 'BTST loop doubled by item 4' (SW leg shortened/widened, loop area no worse, high-side FET soft-switched); id 13's 'brief hard rule 6' citation (rule 6 is 'nothing in series with a flight power path') and its 'checks pass the wrong way' framing (an ISS-open test in Mode 2 fails visibly); attribution of the bypass to fix item 1 (the pre-fix CHG_BAT feed was GND-referenced too).

Sub-claims dropped from rank 7 (id 11): the IPC-2221 internal-curve 86-102 C rise and the proposed 1.5 A interim current cap; 35-52 mW per run 0.21 mm from a GND plane gives ~10 C, and the 20 C criterion belonged to the removed heritage J16.8 path.
Sub-claim dropped from rank 3 (id 14): 'both gates referenced to VSS'; COUT_GATE's low level is V-/B- (EA-165 p.9), so TP504 pairs with TP502. Corrected in rank 3.

Correction recorded against QA rank 2's wording, not against its conclusion: the strip x 250-274, y 168.5-172.5 is not entirely empty; three 0.8 mm vias sit at (250.65,169.1), (254.8,169.1) and (268.95,169.1). All are 1.6-1.9 mm outside the J510 courtyard width (x 256.7-267.3) and there are no tracks on any layer in x 255-270, y 166.5-172.5, so the 2.87 mm move remains a bench-area-only edit. The PCB principal's 'drawing not retrievable' uncertainty is resolved by the chair's own read of the HRO drawing (LCSC C165948 via the flux.ai/storage.googleapis.com mirror; LCSC and krhro.com URLs return HTML).

Not re-reported per PM instruction: first-review next-rev items 8-11 (none made worse by the rework), the 95 deferred track_width residuals (the 0.3 mm VBAT_BENCH_N neck remains the known residual), and item 5 itself beyond the probe additions in rank 5.
